title: नेपाली भाषिक रूपको विश्लेषण
nepali: लेखसार यो लेख उद्देश्यमूलक रूपमा गुणात्मक विधिको उपयोग गरी द्वितीय स्रोतका सामग्रीहरू सङ्कलन गरी नेपाली भाषिक रूपको व्याख्या विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । नेपाली भाषिक शब्दनिर्माणमा प्रयुक्त हुने उपसर्ग, मध्यसर्ग, परसर्ग, व्युत्पादन, रूपायन र व्याकरणिक पक्षमा सहभागी हुने लघुतम   अर्थयुक्त सार्थक एकाइहरू रूप हुन् । रूप मुक्त र बद्घ गरी दुई प्रकारका छन्, जस्तै ः रामले रावणलाई मा¥यो भन्ने वाक्यमा ‘रामले’, ‘रावणलाई’ ‘मा¥यो’ वाक्यका तीनवटा रूपमा ‘राम’, ‘रावण’, ‘मार’्, मुक्त रूप र ‘ले’, ‘लाई’, ‘यो’ बद्घ रूप हुन् । रूप शब्दभन्दा तल्लो वा सबैभन्दा तल्लो भाषिक एकाइ हो । अफ्रिकीमा बोलिने साहिली भाषाको रूप ९ल्ष्तबपगउभलमब० ‘निताकुपेन्डा’को अर्थ ‘म तिमीलाई माया गर्छु’ एउटै रूपका शब्द हुन् तर अङ्ग्रेजीमा यस रूपको ९लष् ˗तब   ˗पग ˗उभलमब० अर्थ ९क्ष्   धष्िि थयग यिखभ० भई चारवटा रूप भएका छन् । रूपविज्ञानलाई अङ्ग्रेजीमा मार्फोलोजी ९ःयचउजययिनथ० भनिन्छ । यो शब्द मार्फ ९ःयचउज० र ९ीयनयक० ग्रीक भाषाका दुई शब्दबाट निर्माण भएको हो । पाणिनिले पदलाई ‘सुबन्त र तिङन्त’ गरी दुई भागमा विभाजन गरेका छन् । शब्दका रूपायक प्रत्ययलाई ‘सुप्’ र धातुमा जोडिने प्रत्ययलाई ‘तिङ्’ विभक्तिले चिनिन्छ । रूपविश्लेषण (क) एकाइ र समायोजन (ख) एकाइ र पक्रिया (ग) शब्द र रूपावली पद्घतिको आभारमा गरिन्छ । यस लेखमा भाषिक शब्द संरचनामा प्रयुक्त हुने लघुतम सार्थक एकाइका रूपहरूमा मुक्त, बद्घ, कोशीय, व्याकरणिक, रिक्त र शून्य रूपका प्रकारहरू व्याख्या विश्लेषण गरी देखाइएको छ ।
american_english: Abstract: In this article, by purposively utilizing a qualitative method and collecting materials from secondary sources, the Nepali linguistic morpheme has been explained and analyzed. The minimal meaningful units that are used in prefixes, infixes, and suffixes in Nepali linguistic word formation and participate in derivation, inflection, and grammatical aspects are morphemes. Morphemes are of two types, free and bound; for example, in the sentence 'Ramle Ravanlai maryo' [Ram killed Ravana], among the three word-forms in the sentence, 'Ramle', 'Ravanlai', and 'maryo', 'Ram', 'Ravan', and 'mar' are free morphemes, while '-le', '-lai', and '-yo' are bound morphemes. A morpheme is a linguistic unit below a word, or the lowest linguistic unit. In the Swahili language spoken in Africa, the form (Nitakupenda) 'Nitakupenda' with the meaning 'I love you' is a single word form, but in English, this form (ni-ta-ku-penda) with the meaning (I will love you) consists of four morphemes. Morphology is called 'morphology' (Morphology) in English. This word is formed from two Greek words, 'morph' (Morph) and (Logos). Panini divided the inflected word (pada) into two categories: 'subanta' [nominal] and 'tinganta' [verbal]. Inflectional suffixes of words are identified as 'sup' affixes, and affixes attached to verbal roots are identified as 'ting' inflections. Morphemic analysis is conducted on the basis of (a) item and arrangement, (b) item and process, and (c) word and paradigm frameworks. In this article, among the forms of minimal meaningful units utilized in linguistic word structure, the types of free, bound, lexical, grammatical, empty, and zero morphemes have been explained, analyzed, and illustrated.

informal_english: Abstract: Right, so this paper deliberately uses qualitative methods, rounding up secondary sources to pull apart and explain the Nepali linguistic morpheme. Morphemes are basically the tiniest meaningful units you get in prefixes, infixes, suffixes, derivation, inflection, and the whole grammar side of Nepali word-building. You have two kinds of morphemes, free and bound; take the sentence 'Ramle Ravanlai maryo' [Ram killed Ravana], where out of the three bits—'Ramle', 'Ravanlai', and 'maryo'—'Ram', 'Ravan', and 'mar' are free morphemes, while '-le', '-lai', and '-yo' are bound ones. A morpheme is smaller than a proper word, pretty much the lowest linguistic unit going. In African Swahili, the single word (Nitakupenda) 'Nitakupenda' means 'I love you', but when you look at it in English, that same form (ni-ta-ku-penda) meaning (I will love you) splits into four separate morphemes. In English, the study of morphemes is called 'morphology' (Morphology). The word itself comes from a pair of Greek words, 'morph' (Morph) and (Logos). Panini went and divided words into two lots: 'subanta' [nominals] and 'tinganta' [verbals]. The inflectional endings on words are known as 'sup' suffixes, and whatever attaches to verbal roots gets called 'ting' inflections. Analysing morphemes is done using (a) item and arrangement, (b) item and process, and (c) word and paradigm approaches. And in this paper, among those minimal meaningful units in word structure, free, bound, lexical, grammatical, empty, and zero morphemes are all properly broken down, analysed, and laid out.
